newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '97 GDP growth seen 7.99 pct-Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '97 GDP growth seen 7.99 pct-Reuter poll.

text.p: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to slow down a bit further next year in line with the government's forecast, analysts said.
In a poll by Reuters, 16 large research houses forecast an average 7.99 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1997 against the government's 8.0 percent.
They forecast the 1996 GDP growth at an average 8.08 percent against the government's expectation of 8.2 percent announced in the Economic Report for 1996/97.
The country reported a GDP growth of 9.5 percent in 1995.
Ten of those polled also provided predictions for the fourth quarter of 1996 and first quarter of 1997.
They forecast an average GDP growth of 7.91 percent in the fourth quarter of this year against 8.0 percent reported in the third quarter and 9.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1995.
In the first quarter of 1997, the economy is expected to grow at 8.01 percent against 8.3 percent in corresponding period of 1995, according to the poll.
